items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: who is a pianist, and he's turned actor -- as a matter of fact, he's had some acting parts in pictures now, I understand; a very good friend.

ctx.x: whose name I can't remember... Everybody used to call him Dr. Fu(?). I can't remember his name. But he and, as I said, Joe Eldridge. There was a fellow named Roswell Gayle(?), who is in California now, who is a pianist, and he's turned actor -- as a matter of fact, he's had some acting parts in pictures now, I understand; a very good friend. There was a guy who was playing bass, and he was a former saxophone player. I can't remember his name either. He smoked a cigar a lot. But anyway, they were there with Roy…

I don't know... Each one of those places had at least two bands. The Preview was on Randolph Street, and we were on State Street. Right down the street from Roy Eldridge, on the right, was a guy who later became a very famous accordion player, whose name was Art Van Damme. He had one of the most popular ever accordion trios, and he used to be fantastic on the accordion. Down the street from him was the band that recorded Dizzy's...
